data.Description: Crisp, mild cucumbers perfect for slicing, salads, and refrigerator pickles. Incredibly productive once they get going — harvest often to keep the plants pumping. One of the most rewarding vegetables in the summer garden.

Buttery yellow summer squash with smooth skin and tender flesh. Harvest when small for the best flavor. Incredibly productive — check the plants daily in midsummer or you’ll be finding baseball bats under the leaves.

Crisp, blocky pickling cucumbers bred for crunch and brine flavor. Dark-skinned 4–5 inch fruits hold up beautifully in vinegar or fermented brine. Plant, pick daily, and fill your jars. One of the most satisfying summer harvests.

Compact mini sweet peppers in a mix of red, yellow, and orange. Incredibly crunchy and sweet — perfect for snacking, stuffing, or packing in lunchboxes. Much more productive than full-size bells in Pittsburgh’s summers.

Serious heat with serious flavor — fruity and floral with a slow, intense burn. The classic hot sauce and Caribbean cooking pepper. Not for the faint of heart, but incredibly satisfying for heat lovers.

A sweet Italian frying pepper with paper-thin walls and extraordinary sweetness — originally from Basilicata, Italy. Sauté with olive oil and they practically melt into a sweet, silky sauce. One of our favorite peppers on the farm.
Hotter and brighter than a jalapeño — crisp, clean heat that works beautifully in salsas, fresh sauces, and pico de gallo. Pick green or let ripen to red for a deeper, slightly smoky flavor.
One of the world’s hottest peppers, with a fruity, floral aroma before the heat hits hard. Grow for extreme hot sauce or just for the bragging rights. Handle with gloves — this one is not a joke.

Mild to medium heat with thick walls and excellent pickled flavor. Sweet when yellow, hotter as it ripens to red. A Pittsburgh backyard garden classic — great for frying, stuffing, or packing into vinegar brine pickles.

The legendary ghost pepper (Bhut Jolokia) — one of the hottest peppers on earth with an intense fruity aroma before the heat wallops you. Use sparingly in hot sauces or dried spice blends. Wear gloves.
Green-striped salad specialty. A delicious, tangy salad tomato, ripe just as the green fruit develops a yellow blush, accentuating the darker green stripes. ...

A beloved heirloom paste tomato from Amish communities right in our region. Large, meaty fruits with few seeds and rich, concentrated flavor. Excellent for sauce, roasting whole, or eating fresh off the vine.

The legendary Italian plum tomato — meaty, low-moisture flesh with bright acidity and deep, rich flavor. Widely considered the gold standard for sauce and canning. Our strain produces large, elongated fruits on vigorous vines.

The dependable, classic paste tomato. Dense, meaty flesh with low moisture and few seeds — perfect for sauce, salsa, and sun-drying. Determinate plants produce a heavy set all at once, ideal for batch canning.

An early-maturing determinate cherry tomato that sets heavy crops of round, deep-red fruits. Great for smaller gardens where you want a reliable, compact plant that doesn’t need constant staking.

One of the earliest cherry tomatoes you can grow — golden yellow fruits with a sweet, well-balanced flavor. Compact determinate plants are perfect for containers or small beds. Ready weeks before larger varieties.

The classic sweet red cherry tomato that gardeners have grown for decades. Long, dangling clusters of bite-sized fruits that just keep coming all summer. Great for snacking, salads, and slow-roasting.

Delicate, pale yellow cherry tomatoes with a mild, sweet flavor. A conversation starter at the table — people always ask what they are. Lower acid than red varieties, gentle enough for sensitive stomachs.
Intense fruity flavor. Exceptionally sweet, bright tangerine-orange cherry tomatoes leave everyone begging for more. Vigorous plants start yielding early and ...

Rich, complex flavor — sweet with an earthy depth unlike any other cherry tomato. Deep purple-brown skin with dark interior. One of the most flavorful cherries we grow, and a showstopper on any plate.

A small elongated grape tomato that’s incredibly crack-resistant and prolific. Juliet produces heavy clusters of meaty, sweet-tart fruits that hold beautifully on the vine for weeks. Very easy to grow, very forgiving.
Gorgeous bi-color grape tomato — golden-yellow with a rosy blush. Sweet, fruity flavor with low acidity. Prolific and holds well on the vine. Stunning on a cheese board or caprese plate.
Classic Italian-style eggplant with the deep purple, elongated shape you know from the kitchen. Excellent for eggplant Parmesan, grilling, and roasting. Smooth, creamy flesh when cooked.

A chunkier, rounder Italian eggplant with thicker walls and meatier flesh than elongated types. Holds its shape beautifully when grilled, baked, or stuffed. Great for caponata and stuffed eggplant recipes.

Sweet garden peas — one of the first things you can plant in spring. Crisp, tender pods that are best eaten straight off the vine. Plant out early and enjoy the harvest before summer heat arrives. Kids love picking and eating them fresh.

Bold, spicy basil with a licorice-anise note essential in Thai curries, pho, and stir-fries. More heat-tolerant than Italian basil and slower to bolt. Beautiful purple stems and flowers make it ornamental too.
The classic Italian basil — large, fragrant leaves with that signature sweet, peppery perfume. The one for fresh pesto, caprese, and finishing pasta. Grow a lot; you’ll use all of it.

A kitchen essential — snip over eggs, potatoes, sour cream, or anything that needs a mild, fresh onion note. Perennial in Zone 6b, so plant once and harvest for years. Produces beautiful edible purple flowers in spring.

Classic culinary thyme — earthy, herby, essential for roasted meats, soups, and Mediterranean cooking. Low-maintenance perennial that comes back stronger every year in Pittsburgh’s climate. Smells incredible in the garden.

Fragrant, beautiful perennial lavender. Grow for cutting, drying, baking, and making sachets. Long-blooming with silver-green foliage that looks stunning all season. Attracts pollinators heavily — bees cannot resist it.
Popular, multipurpose perennial. Semidouble blooms in shades of lavender, salmon, magenta, and pale to bright pinks are useful as cut and edible flowers. ...

Intensely fragrant herb with broad, soft leaves. The warm, earthy scent is used in perfumery, incense, and aromatherapy. Needs full sun and warmth — grow as an annual in Pittsburgh and dry the leaves for sachets and potpourri.

The essential herb for French cooking — long, slender leaves with a distinctive anise flavor. Perfect for chicken, fish, béarnaise sauce, and herb butters. Mild, refined, and unlike anything else in the herb garden.

Also called Mexican mint marigold — a fragrant herb that tastes remarkably like tarragon but handles summer heat far better. Use just like French tarragon in cooking. Produces small yellow flowers late in the season.

The quintessential pickle herb, and so much more. Fresh dill transforms potato salads, cucumber salads, and salmon. Let it flower for beautiful lacy umbels that attract beneficial insects. Our slow-bolt variety stays leafy longer than most.

Fast-growing herb essential in salsa, tacos, and most fresh Latin and Asian dishes. Our slow-bolt variety stays leafy longer than standard types — but once temps climb, let it flower for coriander seed, which is equally useful.

Wheat grass grown for cats — a tasty, safe indoor green that satisfies their instinct to graze and may help reduce hairballs. Grow in a pot and set near their favorite spot. Fresh and ready to nibble within days of sprouting.

Cheerful, edible flowers in shades of orange, red, and yellow — peppery and beautiful. Toss the blossoms in salads or use as garnishes. The leaves taste like mild arugula. Trailing habit is gorgeous in containers and hanging baskets.

Long-blooming globe amaranth with bold, papery flower heads in vivid pinks, purples, and reds. Heat and drought tolerant — keeps blooming all summer when other flowers slow down. Excellent for fresh and dried arrangements.

Big, vibrant blooms that put on a show from midsummer until frost. Zinnias are one of the best cutting garden flowers — the more you cut, the more they bloom. Pollinators absolutely love them. Easy to grow, impossible to kill.
Classic cornflowers. Deep blue. Upright plants produce abundant double and semidouble, 1–1 1/2" blooms. Prefers cool temperatures. Overall ...

Classic cheerful sunflowers in a honey-peach palette — softer and more elegant than traditional bright yellow. Single-stem variety produces one large bloom per plant. Gorgeous in cutting arrangements and as a garden focal point.

Ready-to-fruit mushroom block — no substrate prep needed. Just mist, wait, and harvest. Our blocks are fully colonized and ready to produce their first flush right out of the bag. Perfect for anyone who wants the joy of growing mushrooms without starting from scratch.

Easy, productive bush beans that deliver a heavy crop of classic green beans. Compact plants need no staking — just plant, water, and pick. Perfect for fresh eating, blanching and freezing, or summer salads.
Crisp, sweet snap peas you can eat pod and all — one of the most satisfying things to grow. Plant early in spring for a late spring harvest. Great for kids to pick and eat straight from the vine.

Classic mild Italian pepperoncini — the little yellow-green pepper that makes hoagies and Italian subs. Thin-walled and mildly tangy with just a touch of heat. Pickle them in vinegar brine or eat fresh. A Pittsburgh sandwich staple.

The authentic Mexican tomatillo — green-husked, tangy, and perfect for fresh salsa verde. Toma Verde turns bright green when fully ripe and practically falls off the plant when ready to harvest. Grown outdoors, it produces abundantly all season. A staple ingredient in traditional Mexican cooking and a fun, easy crop for adventurous home cooks.
data.Growing_Tips: Plant two or more for pollination. Harvest when husk turns papery and slightly splits. Great in salsa verde, green chile, and roasted sauces.

data.Description: A treasured heirloom with a devoted following — Aunt Molly's Ground Cherry wraps each golden berry in a papery husk. Sweet with a hint of tropical vanilla, these little gems are delicious fresh, in jams, pies, and salsa. They fall from the plant when ripe and can be stored in their husks for weeks. Once you try them, you'll plant them every year.
data.Growing_Tips: Harvest when berries fall naturally to the ground. Leave husks on for storage — they keep for weeks. Excellent for jams, desserts, and fresh eating.

data.Description: Striking kale with deep purple-red stems and dark green leaves — one of the most beautiful plants in the garden. Slightly more tender than curly kale. Lovely in salads when young; excellent braised or sautéed when mature.

Upright, crisp romaine heads with thick ribs and crunchy leaves. The backbone of a great Caesar salad. Tolerates a bit more heat than other lettuce types — a reliable producer for the Pittsburgh growing season.
Soft, silky butter lettuce with a mild, sweet flavor. Beautiful loose heads that look as good as they taste. One of the most elegant salad greens — delicate enough to let dressing shine.
All the crunch of romaine with stunning deep burgundy-red leaves. A showstopper in salads and on plates. Great flavor and beautiful enough to use as a garnish or edible decoration.
Extra-crunchy lettuce with a juicy snap and clean, refreshing flavor. Holds up well in salads without wilting quickly. Great in sandwiches and wraps.
The same great crunch as Sweet Crisp with gorgeous red-tinged leaves. Beautiful in mixed salads alongside green varieties. Mild flavor that appeals to everyone.

Classic Southern cooking green with large, smooth leaves. Cold-hardy and sweet after frost — perfect for braising, soups, and stir-fries. One of the most nutritious greens you can grow. Easy for beginners.
data.Growing_Tips: Direct sow or transplant after last frost. Harvest outer leaves continuously. Tastes sweeter after a frost. Cold-hardy to zone 6b.

data.Description: Classic cottage garden favorites with tall, colorful spikes that bloom all season. Our Rocket Mix snapdragons come in a gorgeous blend of reds, pinks, yellows, oranges, and whites — perfect for cutting gardens and bouquets. They thrive in cooler weather and make excellent early-season cut flowers.
data.Growing_Tips: Plant in full sun. Loves cool weather — blooms best in spring and fall. Deadhead regularly to extend bloom time. Great for cutting and bouquets.

data.Description: A tall, stately yarrow with brilliant golden-yellow flower clusters that dry beautifully for arrangements. Parker Yarrow is a pollinator magnet — bees and butterflies flock to it all season. Extremely drought-tolerant once established, with feathery, fragrant foliage. Fresh or dried, these bold blooms add stunning texture to bouquets.
data.Growing_Tips: Very low maintenance once established. Drought tolerant. Cut flowers before fully open for best vase life. Excellent for drying — hang upside down in a cool, dark place.

data.Description: A stunning departure from traditional black-eyed Susans — Sahara Rudbeckia blooms in a warm palette of mahogany, bronze, terracotta, gold, and bicolor petals. Each flower is uniquely patterned, making mixed bouquets truly one-of-a-kind. Long vase life, heat and drought tolerant, and absolutely beloved by bees and butterflies.
data.Growing_Tips: Thrives in heat and tolerates drought. Deadhead to encourage continuous blooming. Cut when the petals are just beginning to open for the best vase life. Great for pollinators.

data.Description: Unlike single-stem sunflowers, these branching varieties produce dozens of blooms per plant all season long — perfect for cutting gardens. Our Summer Breeze Mix offers a warm blend of golden yellows, rich oranges, and bi-colors with pollen-free centers that won't drop on your table. A must-have for flower CSA members and bouquet lovers.
data.Growing_Tips: Plant in full sun with room to spread. Pinch the main stem early to encourage branching. Cut when the outer petals just open for longest vase life — they can last 10+ days.

data.Description: A show-stopping marigold with rich, burnt orange petals edged in brilliant gold — one of the most striking marigolds you'll ever grow. Queen Sofia is an All-America Selections winner for a reason: it blooms early, blooms constantly, and holds its color beautifully in bouquets. Long vase life and excellent for companion planting to deter pests.
data.Growing_Tips: Thrives in heat. Deadhead to encourage continuous blooming. Excellent companion plant — repels deer, rabbits, and many common garden pests. Great for cutting.

data.Description: Big, bold, and brilliant — Giant Orange marigolds produce enormous 4-inch blooms in a vibrant, pure orange that commands attention in the garden. Tall plants make them ideal for the back of borders and for cutting. They're incredibly easy to grow, practically pest-proof, and bloom non-stop from summer through frost.
data.Growing_Tips: Plant in full sun for best blooming. Tolerates heat and some drought. Pinch back early to encourage bushy growth. Works great as a border plant and natural pest deterrent.

data.Description: Three colors, one planting — our Snap Bean Mix includes green, yellow wax, and purple snap beans for the most visually stunning harvest in the garden. All varieties are stringless, tender, and incredibly productive. Kids love picking them straight from the vine. Great for container growing and small-space gardens. The purple beans turn green when cooked!
data.Growing_Tips: Direct sow or transplant after last frost. Keep well-watered for best production. Harvest frequently when pods are young and tender to keep plants producing. Fun for kids!
